editorial:
Imagine being dropped right into the middle of one of the most shocking moments in American history. You get to see the legal battle of Lt. William Calley, the man blamed for the My Lai massacre during the Vietnam War. It feels less like a movie and more like you are sitting in the courtroom watching a real trial unfold. The vibe is heavy and tense because it deals with hard questions about who is actually to blame when things go wrong in war. You will see the clash between the soldiers who just followed orders and the officers who gave them.

What really works here is the acting, which keeps you locked in even though most of the movie is just people talking in a room. The pacing is steady, and it does a great job showing the frustration of the witnesses. While it might feel a bit slow if you want explosions, it is a powerful look at justice.
endingExplained: At the end, Calley is found guilty of murdering civilians and is sentenced to life in prison. However, the real twist is how the politics play out. The movie shows that while Calley took the fall, many people felt the higher-up officers got off too easy. It wraps up by leaving you to think about whether one man should carry the guilt for a whole army's failure.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves history, legal dramas, or true crime stories.
